meta.title: Lawn mowing in Burton, MI | Grand Scapes
meta.description: Grand Scapes mows Burton, MI lawns weekly: mowed, trimmed, edged and blown off, timed to slow spring ground and finished clean along the ditches and walks.

hero.title: The lawn and the ditch, **mowed weekly.**
hero.lede: Grand Scapes mows Burton lawns on a set day each week: cut, trimmed along the house and fences, edged at the walk and drive, and blown off before we leave. You get clean stripes in the grass and a walk and drive clear of clippings.

local.title: What Burton lawns need **from a weekly cut.**
local.intro: Most lawns here were seeded around homes built in the 1950s and 60s, on heavy soil that drains slowly. The grass is thick where it gets sun, the ground stays soft after a rain, and many streets have an open ditch instead of a curb. Each of those changes how a weekly cut should go.

points.title: Soft ground after rain
points.body: Much of this ground holds water after a rain. MSU Extension warns that turning a mower on saturated soil can pack it and tear the turf, so on a wet week we widen the turns and mow the soggy corner last.

points.title: Ditches instead of curbs
points.body: Plenty of Burton streets drain to an open ditch. We mow the bank where the slope and footing allow it, trim the rest by hand, and keep clippings out of the ditch line so it keeps draining.

points.title: Mow high, take a third
points.body: MSU Extension puts current home lawn heights between 2 and 3.75 inches and says never to cut more than a third of the blade at once. In a fast May, some lawns need more than one cut a week, and we will tell you if yours does.

points.title: Overgrown yard complaints
points.body: Burton handles overgrown yards by complaint: a ten day notice, then a ticket or a city cleanup billed to the owner. A standing weekly cut keeps the grass short even in a month you are out of town.

logistics.title: How weekly mowing runs in Burton.
body: Rob comes out first, walks the lawn with you and quotes the season. Once you say go, you get a set day, and the crew shows up on it every week with zero turn mowers, trimmers and blowers on the trailer.

Every visit follows one routine: mow, trim around the house, beds, trees and fences, edge the walks and the drive, then blow the hard surfaces clean. Clippings go back onto the lawn, which MSU Extension recommends because they break down fast and do not cause thatch.

When the yard also needs a [spring cleanup](/spring-cleanup-burton-mi/) or [leaf removal](/leaf-removal-burton-mi/), the same crew handles it, so one call covers the season from the first cut to the last.

faq.q: Do you mow lawns in Burton, MI?
faq.a: Yes. Grand Scapes mows residential lawns in Burton every week on a set day. Each visit includes mowing, trimming, edging and blowing off the walks and drive. The estimate is free: call [(810) 990-3040](tel:+18109903040) or [text Rob](sms:+18109903040).

faq.q: How high should I mow my lawn in Michigan?
faq.a: Most home lawns do well between 2 and 3.75 inches, according to MSU Extension, and taller grass shades the soil and holds back crabgrass. Just as important, never take more than a third of the blade in one cut. We set the deck to the lawn and the season.

faq.q: Can you mow the ditch in front of my house?
faq.a: Usually, yes. Many Burton streets drain to an open ditch, and we mow the bank where the slope and footing allow, then trim what a mower should not reach. Clippings stay out of the ditch so it can carry water.

Most weeks, no. MSU Extension says clippings do not add to thatch and should go back on the lawn when no more than a third is cut at a time. When the grass gets ahead in a wet spring, or leaves start falling, we bag as the yard needs it.

faq.q: What happens if my lawn gets too tall in Burton?
faq.a: After a valid complaint, the city sends a ten day notice, and if nothing changes the owner can be ticketed or billed for a city cleanup. A weekly cut keeps the lawn well short of that point.
